topics.title: Quebec vote puts PQ back in power
topics.summary: Quebec's separatist Parti Quebecois won the provincial election but fell short of a majority, setting up a minority government and new national unity conversations in Canada.
topics.discussionPrompt: When an election changes the whole mood of a province, who starts gaming out the next referendum and who just wants the roads fixed first?

topics.title: Physics Nobel goes to neutrino pioneer
topics.summary: Francis Halzen won the 2026 Nobel Prize in physics for work tied to IceCube, the Antarctic observatory that studies high-energy neutrinos from space.
topics.discussionPrompt: If the universe sends tiny mystery particles through Antarctic ice, who wants the science lecture and who just wants to hear the weirdest fact?

topics.title: Kenya confirms first Ebola case
topics.summary: Kenyan officials confirmed the country's first imported Ebola case and launched contact tracing, while the WHO said it is supporting containment efforts.
topics.discussionPrompt: When public health teams have to move fast, who trusts the checklist and who starts asking how contact tracing actually works?

topics.title: Paramount closes Warner takeover
topics.summary: Skydance-owned Paramount completed its Warner Bros. Discovery takeover, creating a larger entertainment company that brings major studios, streamers and networks under one roof.
topics.discussionPrompt: When two entertainment giants merge, who predicts better shows and who immediately worries every subscription price is about to get spicy?

topics.title: Supreme Court weighs climate lawsuits
topics.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court heard arguments over whether local governments can sue energy companies in state court for climate-related costs.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a city says climate damage hit its budget, who thinks courts should sort it out and who thinks lawmakers should handle it?

topics.title: Measles outbreak prompts emergency order
topics.summary: Pennsylvania's measles outbreak passed 1,000 cases, and New York declared a disaster emergency to expand vaccine and testing access.
topics.discussionPrompt: When an old disease comes roaring back, who reaches for the public health history book and who asks what changed recently?

topics.title: Ofcom investigates Instagram Instants
topics.summary: UK regulator Ofcom opened an investigation into whether Meta properly assessed illegal-content risks around Instagram's Instants sharing feature.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a social app adds a fast new sharing feature, who says move quickly and who wants the safety review before launch day?

topics.title: South Africa eyes 2036 Olympics
topics.summary: South Africa was named among countries preparing to present a case to host the 2036 Olympics, a bid that could bring the Games to Africa for the first time.
topics.discussionPrompt: If Africa hosted its first Olympics, who gets excited about the symbolism and who immediately starts planning the venues and transport map?

topics.title: US water bills keep rising
topics.summary: A new analysis found household drinking-water bills among major U.S. systems rose about 62% over the past decade, outpacing inflation and income growth.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a basic utility gets more expensive every year, who blames old pipes, who blames policy, and who starts checking the bill line by line?

topics.title: AI worries top brand risk list
topics.summary: A new survey reported that misuse of artificial intelligence has become a leading reputational concern for brands as companies race to adopt the technology.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a company says it is using AI responsibly, who wants receipts and who thinks the real test is what happens when something goes wrong?
